title: miND Pipeline AWS EC2 Installation and Setup
author: Andreas B Diendorfer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3f6qjre

steps.title: Launch AWS EC2 Instance
steps.instruction: Launch a new AWS EC2 instance and connect via SSH using the following specifications:

substeps.instruction: Use the most recent Amazon Linux 2 AMI (e.g., kernel v5.1 based).
Select a compute-optimized instance; c5.xlarge is recommended for a good CPU-to-memory ratio.
Allocate at least 50GB SSD storage for average NGS analysis projects (24-48 samples).

steps.title: Install Required Tools
steps.instruction: Update the system package manager and install essential utilities.

substeps.instruction: Update the yum database: `sudo yum update`
Install wget and git: `sudo yum -y install wget git`

steps.title: Clone miND Pipeline
steps.instruction: Clone the miND pipeline repository from GitHub to the home directory.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to home: `cd ~`
Clone the repository: `git clone https://github.com/tamirna/miND.git`
Enter the directory: `cd ~/miND`

steps.title: Configure and Build Data Repository
steps.instruction: Set up the genomic data repository (bowtie indices for genomes, miRNAs, and other RNA species).

substeps.instruction: If using species other than Homo Sapiens or Mus Musculus, edit the `config.yml` files in the `repository/genomes`, `repository/mirbase`, and `repository/rnacentral` subfolders with the required URLs and details.
Navigate to the repository folder: `cd ~/miND/repository/`
Execute the build script: `./build.sh` (this installs dependencies like conda and snakemake during the first run).

steps.title: Synchronize Pipeline Configuration
steps.instruction: Ensure the main pipeline configuration matches the built repository data.

substeps.instruction: Open `miND/config.yml` and verify that the genomeIDs, code, genomeVersion, and txid are identical to those in the `repository/data` directory.

steps.title: Prepare Project Data and Sample Sheet
steps.instruction: Organize the project-specific raw data and the SampleContrastSheet.xlsx file.

substeps.instruction: Create a data folder outside the miND directory (e.g., `~/data/[ProjectName]`).
Store raw data files (supported types: fastq/fq, fastq.gz/fq.gz, and bam without alignments) in this project subfolder.
Place the `SampleContrastSheet.xlsx` file in the same folder as the raw data.
Configure the `SampleContrastSheet.xlsx` file, ensuring raw data filenames are relative to the sheet's location and project details in the first sheet are completed.

steps.title: Execute miND Pipeline
steps.instruction: Run the pipeline using the provided wrapper script.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to the miND directory: `cd ~/miND`
Execute the pipeline by providing the path to the sample sheet: `./run.sh ../data/[ProjectName]/[ProjectName]_SampleContrastSheet.xlsx`
Note: Use `./run.sh --help` to view additional options.

steps.title: Retrieve and Evaluate Results
steps.instruction: Locate the output files and analyze the results.

substeps.instruction: Find the results in the `output/[ProjectName]` directory.
Locate the final .zip file containing `multiQC.html`, `report.html`, and the used `SampleContrastSheet`.
Review `multiQC.html` for sequencing quality and `analysis.html` for result download links (e.g., count tables).
If rerunning the pipeline with the same data, delete the output folder first to ensure all data is regenerated.
